sections.title: Sound of the letter U
paragraphs: The letter (U) /uː/ is called /uː/. Its main sound is heard in the word (Uhr) /uːɐ̯/, which means clock or watch. This letter makes two different sounds in German. Both sounds are simple vowels.

sections.title: How to say the letter U
paragraphs: For the long sound, pull your tongue back. Push your lips forward into a small, tight circle. Let your voice hum steadily. For the short sound, open your mouth a little wider. Relax your lips slightly. Keep your tongue pulled back. Put a finger before your lips to feel them push forward.

sections.title: Spelling rules for the letter U
paragraphs: Before a single consonant, you make a long sound. You can hear this in (gut) /ɡuːt/. Before two consonants, you make a short sound. You can hear this in (und) /ʊnt/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid with U
paragraphs: Do not let your lips glide into a w sound at the end. In the English word boot, your lips often move. Keep your lips completely still until the sound finishes. Also, do not start with a y sound like in the English word music.
